name: Jonathan
description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Saul chose three thousand men, two thousand with him in Michmash and mount Bethel and a thousand with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it; Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, and Israel was had in abomination with the Philistines. His son popped off the battle, so now it is war time.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

points: So in the day of battle there was neither sword nor spear in the hand of any of the people, but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found; only two men in the army had a blade.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

points: Jonathan said unto the young man that bare his armor, Come, let us go over to the Philistines' garrison on the other side; but he told not his father. Saul tarried under a pomegranate tree in Migron with about six hundred men, with Ahiah the priest wearing an ephod, and the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: Between the passages were two sharp rocks, Bozez and Seneh, one facing Michmash and the other Gibeah. Jonathan said, Come, let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised; it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.

The Lord put that spirit on Jonathan. That is how the Most High operates: he loves to show his power by having a small number defeat a very large number. That is why it will be the 144,000 taking over the whole world; that is just how he rolls.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: Some hold a doctrine that Jonathan was a homosexual; this act answers it. Scaling a rock face to rush a garrison two-deep is a bold, manly act of war that most men are not cut out for; he carried himself like a real man.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, his armor bearer after him, and that first slaughter was about twenty men within about half an acre of land. Two men against a garrison.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: Jonathan dipped the end of his rod in an honeycomb and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes were enlightened; like the first taste after a long fast, he felt like a whole new creature. Then one of the people told him his father straitly charged the people with an oath, and the people were faint.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: Saul said, Draw ye near, all the chief of the people, and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day; for as the Lord liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: Saul said unto the Lord God of Israel, Give a perfect lot; and Saul and Jonathan were taken, but the people escaped. Then they cast lots between Saul and Jonathan, and Jonathan was taken.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: Jonathan told him, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die. And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan. Saul was ready to kill his own son over the oath.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: The people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not; they kept him from the wrath of his father.

Think about the contrast, and why the scripture says to get the love of the congregation. In chapter 13 Saul was the one disobeying the voice of the Lord and getting rebuked, while Jonathan was brave and mighty and had just saved Israel out of the hand of its enemies; now the coward wants to kill the deliverer.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

points: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. I want you to think about this now. The Lord told King Saul that a neighbour of his, one that is better than him, is who the Lord is choosing. David steps up on the scene and drops his resume. Then David kills the Philistine that everyone was afraid of. Now when David returns he has the head of the Philistine in his hand. Jonathan, the king's son, who the Lord has rejected, is now tight with that brother. I want y'all to see how this is progressing. He is now tight with that brother that God says is better than his father.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Address the perversion head on, as we did last class: souls being knit is not talking about anything unnatural between the two men. The same word describes the church: hearts knit together in love, as joints and bands in one body. Jonathan and David were on one accord; they had the same spirit.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

points: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle. Now Jonathan is a king's son, so you know this was the finest garments. Jonathan took off his robe and gave it to David. Imagine the king that obviously paid for or had this tailored, had it made. He then sees this clothing on the brother that just killed the Philistine that everybody is now praising. And he gave him his sword, which it does not say, but could have been given to him by his father. I am not saying it says that, but it could have been. Think about that. What I want you to see is the progression of it.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul, and they made a covenant; Jonathan stripped himself of his robe and gave it to David, with his garments, his sword, his bow, and his girdle.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

points: Saul spake to Jonathan his son and to all his servants that they should kill David. The Philistines could not get him, so now he wants Israelites to kill an Israelite; that is how far down the slope this man has gone.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: But Jonathan delighted much in David and told him: my father seeketh to kill thee; take heed to thyself until the morning, abide in a secret place, and hide thyself. I will commune with my father of thee, and what I see, that I will tell thee.

Jonathan would have been next in line for the throne; you would think his loyalty lay with his daddy, but he saw the spirit was not on his father, it was on his brother David. His loyalty exceeded his own desires. That is the kind of friend to look for, and the lesson to learn from Jonathan.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: Saul hearkened unto Jonathan and sware, As the Lord liveth, he shall not be slain; and Jonathan brought David back to Saul, and he was in his presence as in times past.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

points: That first day Saul spake not anything, for he thought something had befallen David, that surely he was not clean; but on the second day of the month, with David's place empty again, Saul asked Jonathan, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat?

note.label: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon

points: Saul cast a javelin at Jonathan to smite him, whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David; from here the history follows Saul pursuing David.

note.label: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon

points: David asked him how the matter went, and he answered that the people were fled from the battle, many had fallen and were dead, and Saul and Jonathan his son were dead also.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David took hold on his clothes and rent them, and all the men with him did likewise, and they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan, and for the house of Israel that were fallen by the sword.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: David's lament is a prophecy given in the spirit, almost a eulogy: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided; they were swifter than eagles and stronger than lions. Before the devil jumped on Saul he was good, and the two of them were good together.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: Israel's forefathers died only when the Most High said it was time; that is the only way any of them died. David mourned Jonathan, saying his love to him was wonderful, passing the love of women.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

points: Jonathan's son Mephibosheth was lame of his feet. When the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, he was five years old, and his nurse took him up and fled, and in her haste he fell and became lame.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: David asked whether there was yet any left of the house of Saul that he might show him kindness for Jonathan's sake. Remember that Saul's son Jonathan and David were always very close.
That closeness goes back to the beef between Saul and David in the book of Samuel; Jonathan was always there for David, that was David's homeboy, they were really close.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: A servant of the house of Saul named Ziba was brought to David. When David asked whether there was yet any of the house of Saul that he might show the kindness of God unto him, Ziba said Jonathan had yet a son who was lame on his feet, dwelling in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel in Lodebar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: To show his love for Jonathan, David gave everything that Saul owned to Jonathan's son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: When Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan came unto David he fell on his face and did reverence. David told him, Fear not, for I will surely show thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father, and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

note.label: 2 Samuel 9: David Shows Kindness for Jonathan's Sake

points: The king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the Lord's oath that was between David and Jonathan. David did not go back on his oath; earlier he had promised Jonathan that his seed would always eat at David's table as long as there was family of the lineage of Jonathan.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: Jonathan's body had been hanged in the temple of Dagon, the fish god of the Hamites. David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father, and performed all that the king commanded. After that the Most High was entreated for the land.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: The chapter returns to Gibeon and repeats the line of Ner, Kish, and Saul, tracing Saul's sons and the house of Jonathan down through Micah to Azel.
